abstract: The OECD Youth Employment Outlook 2025 documents significant labor market challenges for young workers in OECD countries, with youth employment in AI-exposed sectors declining 4.5% year-over-year and real starting salaries falling 3-8% across knowledge-work sectors, indicating substantial disruption to early-career employment and compensation.
keyFindings: Youth (18-24) employment in OECD countries in AI-exposed sectors declined 4.5% year-over-year.
Real starting salaries fell 3-8% across knowledge-work sectors.
methodology: Not specified. Appears to be analysis of OECD employment data for youth ages 18-24 across member countries, with focus on AI-exposed sectors and knowledge-work sectors, but specific data sources, sample scope, and analytical methods are not described in the provided excerpt.
